clue.text: Rush manuscript to female Arab quarters

parts.note: to rush is to hare, dash along

explanation.surface: Someone hurries a document across to the women's rooms of an Arab household.
explanation.definitionFit: A harem is the secluded women's section of a traditional Muslim household.

clue.text: Dislike crossing building site, and temporise

indicators.note: crossing means the first word spans the other, with it inside

parts.note: to dislike strongly is to hate

indicators.note: building means the letters of site are put together in a new form

explanation.surface: Someone who hates walking over a construction site stalls for time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dislike crossing' reads like a phobia of road crossings, but 'crossing' means straddling: HATE spans ESIT, the shuffled SITE that 'building' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay or stall to gain time, to waver.

clue.text: Fruit is found in monsoons

indicators.note: found in tells us the short word sits within the weather word

parts.note: monsoons are seasonal rains
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit grows in the rainy season.
explanation.definitionFit: Raisins are dried grapes, a dried fruit.

clue.text: Misses the atmosphere of town

parts.note: misses are young unmarried women, maids
the atmosphere of a place is its tone

explanation.surface: Young women miss the feel of the town.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIDSTONE is the county town of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidstone is an English county town, in Kent.

clue.text: Air Force meal supplier?

parts.note: reads like a military catering contractor, but means a mill that grinds meal (coarse flour) powered by the force of the air

explanation.surface: A caterer that feeds the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: The building's sails are turned by moving air, and the machinery grinds grain into meal.

clue.text: How police train son to be responsible for family

indicators.note: how asks in what manner, so these words are to be arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: How a constabulary trains a boy to support his family.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means in the place of a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase describes someone acting in a parent's place, taking on a guardian's duties.

clue.text: The same can be said in France to…

parts.note: dit is French for said
taken as written

explanation.surface: An identical remark could be made in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the aforesaid thing again, as said before.

clue.text: One with endlessly poor diction-silly!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: poor signals the letters are in bad shape and must be reordered
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone's bad pronunciation sounds foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'diction-silly' hides the join between wordplay and definition; 'endlessly' trims the word and 'poor' reorders the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means very foolish or stupid.

clue.text: Light that shines way into the trap

indicators.note: into puts the road abbreviation inside the word for trap

parts.note: a lure is a bait or trap
ST, street, is a common abbreviation for a way

explanation.surface: A gleam leads someone along the path into a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a soft glow or sheen of reflected light.

clue.text: CV with identical letters to aspiring Arts master

definitions.text: CV with identical letters to aspiring Arts master

parts.words: CV with identical letters to aspiring Arts master
parts.note: describes a two-word phrase with initials C and V whose remaining letters are the same in both words, naming an eager arts enthusiast

explanation.surface: A curriculum vitae written by a would-be Master of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: A person avidly keen on the arts and culture is mockingly compared to a scavenging bird.

clue.text: Sunday's holy ceremony kept holy

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday
pi is slang for pious or holy
a ceremony kept regularly is a ritual

explanation.surface: A Sunday church service observed with due reverence.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword staple for holy; the second 'holy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritual matters are sacred or religious ones, the opposite of worldly.

clue.text: Gets rug in back street

indicators.note: the toupee goes inside the turned street abbreviation
back tells us the street abbreviation is written right to left

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or toupee

explanation.surface: Someone collects a carpet from a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets' is the informal sense of understanding, not acquiring; 'back' reverses the street abbreviation to TS around the WIG.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is informal for understanding, as in 'gets it'.

clue.text: Come top in test fitting-what to wear?

indicators.note: the victory is placed inside the rearranged test letters
a fitting adjusts and rearranges, signalling the letters of test are reworked

parts.note: to come top is to win

explanation.surface: Excelling at a trial run in a clothes shop's changing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitting' looks like a clothes fitting, matching the definition, but it reorders TEST to TSET; a twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A twinset is a matching cardigan and jumper worn together, a classic outfit.

clue.text: Farmer's credit frequently curtailed by end of summer

definitions.note: read as 'farmer is', the singular noun the answer names

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, so the last letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: frequently means often

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, taken from summer here

explanation.surface: A farmer's bank balance is often reduced by the close of the summer season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the final N of OFTEN; 'end of summer' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A crofter works a small tenant farm, mainly in the Scottish Highlands and Islands.

clue.text: Poet captivated by elegant assonance

indicators.note: something held captive by these words sits inside them, running across their letters

explanation.surface: A versifier is charmed by graceful repeated vowel sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian poet, author of Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: A telling off for agent going to fish

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent, short for representative
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A salesman gets scolded for slipping off to go angling.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproach is a rebuke, words expressing disapproval.

clue.text: Exaggerated concerning the wind to the North

parts.note: over can mean about, concerning
a blow is a strong wind
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A report about a gale heading north.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblown means inflated or overstated beyond what is true.

clue.text: Need 24 hours, alas

parts.note: to need is to lack
twenty-four hours is a day

explanation.surface: Wanting a full day, and lamenting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackaday is an archaic exclamation of sorrow or regret.

clue.text: Gate money more than enough to assume control

parts.note: the take is the money taken, such as gate receipts at a match
over means in excess, more than is needed

explanation.surface: Ticket receipts exceed what is needed, letting someone seize the club.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport 'gate money' is the takings from spectators at the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To take over is to seize charge of something from another.

clue.text: Dress, about to go into shock

indicators.note: to go into puts the preposition inside the word for shock

parts.note: to appal is to shock
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Ready to give someone a fright with an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, attire.

clue.text: Old pictures sent back for bonus

parts.note: ex- means former, old

indicators.note: something sent back goes in the reverse direction, so the word for pictures is read backwards

parts.note: pictures as a body of work are art

explanation.surface: Old photographs are returned as a free gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old pictures' suggests vintage photos, but 'Old' is the prefix meaning former, and 'sent back' turns only the word for pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional benefit beyond what is expected.

clue.text: Comparatively tidy docker

definitions.meaning: neater, in better order, the comparative of an adjective for neat
a dock worker who stows and balances coal or cargo in a ship's hold

explanation.surface: A dock worker who keeps a neater yard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the comparative of a word for neat and an old name for a cargo-stowing docker.

clue.text: Get rid of booze!

definitions.meaning: to put an end to, as when one quashes a rumour

explanation.surface: An order to pour away the alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour is to stamp it out; whisky from Scotland is a drink.

clue.text: Financial investment in company in Paris, say

definitions.meaning: the money put into a business by its owners and shareholders
Paris is an example of the chief city of a country

explanation.surface: Money put into a French firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital means both the funds invested in a business and a country's seat of government.

clue.text: Not allowed? Thanks to expression of disapproval

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you
boo is a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: Forbidden? Then gratitude turns to jeering.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is something prohibited by custom.

clue.text: Writer with taste for the old club

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, so a writer
to lick something is to taste it

explanation.surface: An author with a liking for a traditional gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a society, but it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A niblick is an old-fashioned golf club, roughly a modern nine-iron.

clue.text: Though disheartened, take pulse

indicators.note: losing its heart, the word gives up its inner letters and keeps only its opening

parts.note: to rob is to take unlawfully

explanation.surface: Though dispirited, a medic checks someone's heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' usually removes only the centre; here it leaves just the opening TH, as Telegraph setters sometimes allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular beat, like a pulse.

clue.text: Even the editor is not in mufti

parts.note: even means uniform, the same throughout
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Even the newspaper's editor turns up in civilian clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Mufti is plain clothes worn by someone normally in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wearing official dress is the opposite of being in plain civilian clothes.

clue.text: Revered university residence was in debt

parts.note: a hall of residence houses university students
owed means was in debt

explanation.surface: A respected college hostel ran up debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallowed means held sacred and deeply honoured.

clue.text: Go! Listen to why after turning green

indicators.note: after places the next piece behind the rearranged colour
turning means the letters of green twist into a new order
listen to means the word is heard, giving a letter with the same sound

parts.note: the word why is pronounced like the letter Y

explanation.surface: An instruction to set off and ask questions once the lights change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go!' looks like a command, but it is the noun meaning vigour; 'turning' reorders GREEN as ENERG.
explanation.definitionFit: Go as a noun means vigour or drive, as in 'full of go'.
